side_mara: ^The ovens in Ember Row have gone cold twice today. Mara has lit them three times.
^You came back, she says. Good. Hold this.
^She puts a bowl of dough in your hands. It is heavier than it looks.
^The first batch always burns. That is not a failure. That is how you know the oven is awake.
mara_burn: ^You hold the loaf over the flame until the crust goes black. Mara watches without stopping you.
^There, she says. Now the second one is ours.
^The second loaf comes out whole. She tears it in half and gives you the larger piece.
mara_save: ^You pull the loaf early. It is pale in the middle, but it holds.
^Mara laughs. You cannot save everything, she says. But you can save this.
^You eat it standing up, while the ovens cool.
side_iven: ^Iven keeps the Watch ledger in a tin under the checkpoint stair. He has never shown it to anyone.
^These are not orders, he says. These are the people I let go.
^There are more names than pages. Some are crossed out. Some are not.
^The Choir knows this ledger. It has been singing from it.
iven_read: ^You read until your voice gives out. Iven stands at the window and does not turn around.
^When you stop, the Choir answers from below. It knows every name now.
^Good, Iven says. Let it carry them for a while.
iven_burn: ^He holds the tin over the stove. The names curl and go white.
^The Choir screams. It has lost its hymn.
^Iven watches it burn. Then he opens the door.
side_wren: ^Wren is on the Spire roof with a slate and a piece of chalk. She is counting.
^Not bells, she says. Windows. Lit ones.
^Below, Aurel is going dark one street at a time. She counts anyway.
^Four hundred and six, she says. Yesterday it was four hundred and four.
^Ask what happens when the number reaches zero.
wren_count: ^You count until your eyes ache. The number is not the point. The counting is.
^When you finish, she writes the total on her palm and closes her hand around it.
^Four hundred and nine, she says. We are winning.
wren_zero: ^Then we start counting the people, she says. They are harder to see. They are worth more.
^She puts the chalk in your hand. The slate is warm from her holding it.
side_oria: ^The memory garden is in bloom. Oria says that is not a good sign.
^Roses bloom when they are trying to be remembered, she says.
^She walks the rows with a knife, cutting only the flowers that have already begun to fade.
^Ask her to cut a living one.
oria_living: ^She hesitates. Then she cuts the fullest rose in the garden and gives it to you.
^It will not last, she says. That is why it is yours.
^You carry it out of the garden. It does not wilt.
oria_fading: ^You work until the basket is full. Oria does not speak, and neither do you.
^At the gate she touches your sleeve. Remember me as I am, she says. Not as what I keep.
^The garden closes behind you, quieter than before.
side_toma: ^Toma has filled the last page of the ledger. He is staring at the inside cover as if it owes him something.
^I do not know how to write tomorrow, he says.
^The house is quiet. Wren is upstairs. Somewhere below, the city is deciding what to forget.
^Tell him to write what he wants to happen.
toma_blank: ^He draws a line under the last entry and closes the book.
^A blank page is still a page, he says. Tomorrow can be whatever we put there.
^For the first time in nine days, he looks younger than you.
toma_want: ^He writes one line. Then another. He does not let you read them.
^It is not a prophecy, he says. It is a request.
^He closes the book and presses it flat with both hands.
side_vey: ^Vey's sanctuary is empty. The inner door is open, and the dark beyond it is breathing.
^She left this for you, Vey says. A remnant. A last argument.
^Sera Vane steps out of the dark with a pike and no rank left to give orders with.
vey_alone: ^You step forward. Sera does not salute. She does not need to.
^One last order, she says. Survive it.
^The door closes behind you. The pike comes up.
vey_together: ^Vey takes her place at your shoulder. Sera's face does something complicated.
^You brought the keeper, she says. Good. Now it is a fair fight.
^The dark behind the door begins to move.
